_provenance.label: real dunkai output, schema v2 (role-based), GPIO coverage
_provenance.source: dunkai @ 2da5dfc, run.py --requirements (panic-button profile: 2 push buttons, 3 status LEDs)
_provenance.purpose: Targets GPIO specifically. The earlier v2 fixture happened to produce no GPIO edge, leaving allocateGpio() covered only by unit tests. This profile (physical buttons + discrete LEDs) produced GPIO edges on the FIRST attempt -- the architecture prompt maps Buttons -> GPIO and LEDs -> GPIO, so GPIO coverage is reliably reachable this way.

gpio_finding.edges_produced: 2 GPIO nets, BOTH terminating at U1 (the MCU) -- so U1 requires two DISTINCT pads.
gpio_finding.allocation_outcome: allocateGpio() fired and correctly allocated NOTHING. It did not collide with a reserved pad. The catalogue footprint for U1 (STC15F104W-35I-SOP8, jlcpcb:C26928) names only 2 of its 8 pads -- GND=pin4, VCC=pin2 -- and exposes no generic-IO pad to allocate from, so both GPIO requests correctly returned PIN_NOT_FOUND.
gpio_finding.capability_guard: Correctly reported PIN_NOT_FOUND rather than PART_CAPABILITY_MISMATCH: with only 2 of 8 pads named, the absence of a GPIO is NOT confirmed. capabilityCheck.js guard 1 (complete-coverage) working as designed.
gpio_finding.bug_found: This capture exposed a real defect, since fixed: pinMap/pinDetail were keyed `interface/role`, so both GPIO requests on U1 collapsed onto one key "GPIO/GPIO" and the second silently overwrote the first. Same defect class as the chip-select pad collision. Per-net roles (GPIO, CHIP_SELECT) now carry the net name in their key.
gpio_finding.still_unproven: GPIO allocation landing on a real pad remains UNPROVEN on real data. The blocker is catalogue coverage, not the allocator: small MCUs expose almost no functional pin names via extractPinout(). Same source-data limitation as D-054/Phase 6, not a pipeline defect.

known_caveats: eda.py parse_bom_csv calls the live EasyEDA API per BOM row; packages are not offline-reproducible.
U5 (SZYY0402O, an LED) names its pads K/A -- positional, not functional -- so its GPIO request is also PIN_NOT_FOUND.
Architecture agent is non-deterministic; this is one sample, not a guaranteed shape.

recount_2026_08_22_curated_padcount.why: resolver.js's curated branch built its pinout as `{ok, pins}` with no padCount. capabilityCheck needs padCount to assert completeness, so any unresolved pin on a part with a CURATED pinout degraded from PART_CAPABILITY_MISMATCH to PIN_NOT_FOUND. padCount is now taken from the real footprint (never from the curated pins themselves, which are not required to be exhaustive).
recount_2026_08_22_curated_padcount.result_for_this_fixture: UNCHANGED — every count below is identical before and after the fix.
recount_2026_08_22_curated_padcount.reason_unchanged: No component in this fixture has a curated pinout. The curated table holds exactly two parts (LP103SB6F, HY2111-GB) and neither appears here, so the defect could not have affected these numbers. An earlier report claimed this fix would 'change error codes across the fixture set'; that was an overstatement and is corrected here.
recount_2026_08_22_curated_padcount.measured_with: pcb-agent @ the curated-padCount fix, scripts diag over resolveComponents(allowNetwork: true)
